runs.t: Cohesion measures how closely a module's responsibilities belong together; coupling reflects how much it knows about other modules. Good design aims for cohesive units with explicit, limited dependencies.

Group operations around stable domain capabilities and hide internal representations. Prefer dependency direction from application orchestration to stable contracts, measure change impact, and review how many modules must change for one business requirement.

A reservation module should own availability rules and booking transitions. If pricing, authentication, and email templates all live there, cohesion suffers; if every other module writes its tables directly, coupling rises.
Zero coupling is impossible and sometimes undesirable. Overly fine modules with chatty interfaces worsen comprehensibility. Evaluate actual reasons for change rather than counting imports alone.
